title: Stronger rules on third-party litigation funding in consumer claims proposed
summary: The SRA has proposed new requirements for firms that use or arrange third-party litigation funding in consumer claims. These include notifying the SRA, a risk assessment and summary documents for clients.
what_changes: Firms would have to notify the SRA when they use or arrange third-party litigation funding.
Firms would have to produce and keep a third-party litigation funding risk assessment.
Firms would have to give clients summary documents before they sign a third-party funding agreement.
Separate SRA guidance covers current duties on client best interests, independence, conflicts, client information and money laundering.
who_it_applies_to: SRA-regulated firms that use or arrange third-party litigation funding for consumer claims, including high-volume consumer claims.

history.event: Consultation opened, running until 17 September 2026; new guidance on current obligations published at the same time.
